newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria forms coalition govt with new oil minister.
newsitem.headline: Algeria forms coalition govt with new oil minister.

text.p: Algeria named oil expert Youssef Yousfi as new energy minister on Wednesday in a three-party government in which the former foreign, finance and interior ministers kept their jobs, an official statement said.
The government lineup was announced one day before President Liamine Zeroual is to meet the main party leaders to discuss the organisation of local elections planned this year.

Zeroual appeared to be striking a balance between ensuring stability in his violence-torn country, completing an economic reform programme with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and respecting the results of the June 5 election by allowing opposition parties into the cabinet, analysts said.
The coalition confirmed the alliance of moderate Islamists and Zeroual's supporters forged early this week in the country's first multi-party National Assembly (lower house), they added.
Yousfi, a former head of the president's cabinet and ex-top man in the state oil and gas firm Sonatrach, was named energy minister.
OPEC member Algeria relies for more than 90 percent of its hard currency on oil and gas exports and expects to earn around $16 billion from its hydrocarbon exports by the year 2000.
Yousfi replaces Amar Makhloufi in the new cabinet headed by Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia, reappointed nearly two weeks ago by President Liamine Zeroual.

The Islamist-oriented Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS) and former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN) are represented in the cabinet in which the National Democratic Rally (RND), grouping Zeroual supporters, controls the main ministries.
The RND, MPS and FLN emerged as the first parties in this month's general election, winning respectively 156, 69 and 62 seats in the 380-member lower house.
Incumbent Foreign, Interior, Finance and Trade Ministers -- respectively Ahmed Attaf, Mustapaha Benmansour, Abdelkrim Harchaoui and Bakhti Belaib -- were reappointed, the statement said.
Zeroual, following normal Algerian tradition, keeps the defence portfolio.
MPS's main leaders Bougerra Soltani, know as Abu Jarra, and Abdelmajid Menasra are named respectively Small and Medium Enterprise Minister and Industry Minister.
Other MPS officials were appointed as junior ministers.
The FLN, making a comeback after being humiliated in elections in 1990 and 1991 by radical Islamists, held some ministries and secretary of state positions.

The former sole ruling party was thrashed in the first round of the 1991 general election -- Algeria's first multi-party legislative poll -- by the Islamist Salvation Front (FIS). But the authorities cancelled the poll and violence erupted. The FIS was outlawed and could not take part in this month's election.
Prominent FLN members Abderrahmane Belait and Amar Tou were respectively named as equipment minister and universities and scientific research minister.
Algeria is striving to end five and half years of violence and analysts say Zeroual is trying to widen his government base through consensus with the legal opposition.
He is also seeking to advance economic reforms, switching the country to a free market economy after nearly three decades of centralised socialist management.
To try to achieve these ends, the president allowed legal moderate Islamists to compete in the June election and has brought more of them into his government.
About 60,000 people have been killed in the violence since January 1992, while the economy has also been hit by sabotage which officials say cost the country around $2.0 billion.
